input.body:
label: bug
file: src/ingest/parser.ts

The parser splits input on `"
"` only (`text.split("
")`), without stripping carriage returns. Files exported from Windows tools typically use CRLF line endings, so each line (including the header) retains a trailing ``. This causes the column count/shape comparison to mismatch, triggering `errors.rowShape` ("Malformed row...") on row 1 even though the file is well-formed. The parser should normalize line endings (e.g. strip `` or split on `/
|
/`) before splitting into rows.

text: The issue is in `src/ingest/parser.ts` — splitting on `\n` only, not handling Windows CRLF line endings, causing trailing `\r` in header/row columns and mismatched column counts.
